header.contentDescription: How a pin tumbler lock opens: drag along the track to slide the key in; its ridges lift each pin stack until every gap meets the shear line and the plug can turn

text.value: Springs push five pin stacks down. The upper, driver pins cross the shear line, where plug meets housing, and stop the plug turning.
Ridges on the key push each stack up as it passes, then let it fall back. Only a key this shape will do.
Each ridge lifts its stack exactly so the gap between the pins sits on the shear line.
Nothing crosses the shear line now, so the plug turns with the key and pulls the bolt back.
Driver pins cross the shear line.
Ridges lift the pins as it goes.
Every gap is on the shear line.
The plug turns; the bolt retracts.

semantics.contentDescription: Cross-section of a lock: a plug in a housing, five pin stacks held down by springs, a key entering from the left
